review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–360). It has no definitions, no @[simp] or other simp-set attributes, and no custom simp lemmas. Every declaration is an existence or finiteness theorem: exists_isIdempotentElem_notMem_iff, map_maximalIdeal_le_of_isMaximal, exists_isIdempotentElem_notMem_iff_of_moduleFinite, exists_isIdempotentElem_moduleFinite_quotient_notMem, moduleFinite_localization, and solution. None of these is an equation or iff that would be used as a rewrite rule. The simp calls in the proofs are all local `simp only [...]` calls on goals that arise inside those proofs. The file adds no simp interface, so it has no missing canonical simp lemma, no wrong rewrite direction, no competing rules and no loop risk. Recommending simp attributes for the existence statements would be unjustified. I did not look for duplicated Mathlib lemmas, because that is outside this rubric.
